newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Cariplo choses Ambroveneto as bank partner.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Cariplo choses Ambroveneto as bank partner.

text.p: The foundation that controls Italy's largest savings bank Cariplo on Monday voted to open talks on merger with Italian banking group Ambroveneto which could create the nation's largest banking group.

The foundation's central committee that controls the Milan-based Cariplo met on Monday to decide on forming an alliance with either of two Italian banks -- Banco Ambrosiano Veneto (Ambroveneto) or Banca Commerciale Italiana.

The chairman of the foundation, Giuseppe Guzzetti, told journalists that its 18-member board had voted for Cariplo -- whose full name is Cassa di Risparmio delle Provincie Lombarde -- to open merger talks with Ambroveneto.
Guzzetti leaving the meeting said that the committee's decision had been quick and unanimous. "Now we will write to Ambroveneto and say that we are ready to negotiate."
He confirmed there were only two contenders for an alliance with Cariplo, and Guzzetti added he would be happy if a formal draft between the two groups could be drawn up by June 30.

A Cariplo statement said that the central committee had decided to start exclusive talks with Ambroveneto "to study in depth the plan for integration." An Ambroveneto spokesman declined to comment on Cariplo's decision.
Cariplo, which is aiming for a stock market privatisation this year, is being advised in the talks over a banking alliance by U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs.

A Cariplo-Ambroveneto alliance has been hinted in the past, but Banca Commerciale Italiana's (BCI) official interest only came to the fore this weekend when it confirmed its aim of a link-up with Cariplo.
